name: p3-0503-api-down-survives
title: When the API servers are down: what still works and what stops
spec: Two columns on a light background. Left column titled 'Keeps working' (green boxes): 'Running pods (kubelet and runtime continue)', 'kube-proxy keeps existing rules', 'An in-progress multi-node NCCL training job'. Right column titled 'Stops' (red boxes): 'Scheduling', 'Scaling', 'New deployments', 'kubectl', 'Replacing crashed pods that need a controller', 'Autoscalers and operators'. Below, a one-line banner: 'Running workloads do not depend on the control plane being up. Only changes do.' Bottom strip with a small timeline: 'node leases expire after about 40 s' then 'after the 5 min eviction timeout, pods may be evicted when the API returns and nodes look NotReady'. Large text at least 24px.
alt: Two columns show what keeps working and what stops when all API servers are down.
cap: With the API servers down, running pods carry on while every change to the cluster stops.

name: p3-0503-level-vs-edge
title: Level-triggered reconciliation survives a missed event
spec: Two horizontal lanes. Top lane 'Edge-triggered (not Kubernetes)': event 'Pod X just crashed' fires while the controller is restarting, arrow to a grey box 'controller down', result red box 'change missed for good'. Bottom lane 'Level-triggered (Kubernetes)': same event dropped during a network blip or restart, then a box 'Next resync or relist compares current with desired', then 'ReplicaSet wants 4 Pods; 3 exist; create 1', result green box 'converges to the right state'. Footer note: 'Resync is the safety net under every watch.' Text at least 24px.
alt: A missed event is lost for an edge-triggered controller but fixed by the next resync in Kubernetes.
cap: Kubernetes controllers compare current state with desired state, so a dropped event is repaired on the next resync.

name: p3-0503-optimistic-409
title: Two writers and a 409 Conflict
spec: Sequence diagram with three lifelines: 'Client A', 'kube-apiserver / etcd', 'Client B'. Steps numbered: 1 Client A reads object at resourceVersion 5012. 2 Client B reads the same object at resourceVersion 5012. 3 Client B writes its change; server accepts; object now at resourceVersion 5013. 4 Client A writes its change based on 5012; server rejects with HTTP 409 Conflict (red). 5 Client A re-reads the latest version from its informer cache, re-applies its change and retries (green). Side note: 'resourceVersion maps to the etcd key mod_revision' and 'Server-side apply tracks field ownership in managedFields'. Text at least 24px, no crossing arrows.
alt: A stale write based on resourceVersion 5012 is rejected with 409 Conflict and retried.
cap: Optimistic concurrency means the second writer is refused and retries, so neither overwrites the other unknowingly.

name: p3-0503-ownership-finalizer-delete
title: Deleting an object: ownerReferences versus finalizers
spec: Left panel 'ownerReferences (garbage collection)': a chain Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pod with upward arrows labelled 'ownerReference'; a note 'Delete the owner and the garbage collector deletes its dependents' and three small labels 'Foreground', 'Background', 'Orphan' as the deletion propagation policies. Right panel 'finalizers (pre-deletion hooks)': numbered steps 1 'kubectl delete pvc data', 2 'finalizers list not empty, for example kubernetes.io/pvc-protection, so the API server does not delete it', 3 'sets metadata.deletionTimestamp, object is Terminating', 4 'the responsible controller cleans up or waits for Pods that mount the PVC to exit', 5 'controller removes its string from metadata.finalizers', 6 'list empty, API server removes the object from etcd'. Text at least 24px.
alt: Owner references cascade deletion down a chain while finalizers hold deletion until cleanup is done.
cap: ownerReferences drive cascading deletion, and finalizers hold an object in Terminating until a controller finishes cleanup.

name: p3-0503-leader-election
title: Leader election with Lease objects
spec: Three boxes in a row labelled 'control-plane node 1', 'node 2', 'node 3', each with kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager. Node 1 is highlighted 'active leader', nodes 2 and 3 'standby'. Below, a central box 'Lease object in kube-system (coordination.k8s.io/v1)' with arrow from the leader labelled 'renews renewTime every 2 s (retryPeriod)'. Second row after a red X over node 1: 'leader crashes, no renewal within 15 s (leaseDuration)' then arrow 'a standby acquires the Lease and takes over, failover about 15 s'. Note: 'Three active schedulers would cause conflicting bindings and duplicate ReplicaSet creations; API servers stay active-active behind a load balancer'. Command hint 'kubectl get lease -n kube-system'. Text at least 24px.
alt: A leader renews a Lease every 2 seconds and a standby takes over after 15 seconds without renewal.
cap: Scheduler and controller-manager run active-standby, and a missed Lease renewal hands leadership to a standby in about 15 seconds.

name: p3-0503-ports-map
title: Who connects to which port
spec: Hub-and-spoke diagram with kube-apiserver (6443 HTTPS) in the center. Left: 'kubectl, CI, operators' arrow to 6443. Top: 'etcd 2379 client, 2380 peer, mTLS, only API servers are clients' with a double arrow to the API server. Right: 'kube-scheduler 10259' and 'kube-controller-manager 10257' each with an arrow to 6443 labelled 'watch/write'. Bottom: 'kubelet 10250 (healthz 10248 local)' with arrow to 6443 labelled 'watch pods, heartbeat Leases' and a separate arrow from the API server to the kubelet 10250 labelled 'logs, exec, attach, port-forward'. Small boxes: 'kube-proxy 10256 healthz, 10249 metrics', 'NodePort 30000-32767 on all nodes', 'CoreDNS 53 TCP/UDP, 9153 metrics'. Red callout: 'etcd holds every secret; kubelet can run commands in every container on its node'. Text at least 24px.
alt: Hub-and-spoke map of component ports around the API server on 6443.
cap: Every component connects to the API server on 6443, and the API server in turn reaches etcd and the kubelets.
